section.title: EmergencyManagement
section.subtitle: Type: CAT Library: SE.Nereda
section.para: For each reactor, the scheduler maintains a TimeSinceStartFeed value.
This timer runs continuously for each reactor and is reset whenever the corresponding reactor enters the Starting state of the Feed phase.
Example:
The reactors are ordered according to their TimeSinceStartFeed.
The reactor with the highest TimeSinceStartFeed receives the highest feeding priority, because it is the reactor that has been waiting the longest since its previous Feed phase.
This ensures that the reactor which has had the longest available treatment time is selected first.
Example:

section.bridgehead: 3. Feed Interval and Actual Cycle Time
section.para: The nominal Feed Interval is calculated from the configured nominal cycle time and the total number of reactors:

Instead, the Actual Cycle Time is reduced according to the number of available reactors:

section.title: HeartBeat
section.subtitle: Type: CAT Library: SE.Nereda

abstract.para: The HeartBeat block is used to monitor the communication between the PLC and the Nereda controller.

section.para: Communication between the Nereda® Controller and PLC will be monitored by means of a watchdog signal. The control system initiates the first watchdog signal and sends a Boolean signal to the Nereda® Controller.

The HeartBeat block will receive a Boolean signal of 0 or 1 from the Nereda® Controller, and then the HeartBeat block will check the value received from the Nereda® Controller and send back the inverse bit (if the Nereda® Controller sends 1, the HeartBeat will send 0, and vice versa). Every time, the Nereda® Server will send back the same value that the HeartBeat block sent.
In case the HeartBeat does not receive the same value that it sent to the Nereda® Controller within a predefined adjustable ‘watchdog’ time, it will generate a communication failure.

If the Nereda® process control is in "Auto" mode, the emergency recipe is automatically started for each reactor for which the emergency recipe is set to ‘On’. After watchdog communication is restored, the Nereda® process control mode must be switched back to "Auto" or "Manual" by the operator. This is not an automatic action from the process automation system or the Nereda® Controller.

td.para: This Adapter 'IEmergencyON' is used to send the state of the connection between the PLC and the Nereda® Controller through the variable EmergencyOn:

listitem.para: EmergencyOn = TRUE: the connection is lost.
EmergencyOn = FALSE: the connection is good.

EmergencyOn = FALSE: the connection is good.

section.title: Mode
section.subtitle: Type: CAT Library: SE.Nereda

abstract.para: Mode is the block that allows the selection of the operating mode (Automatic, Manual, Emergency) as well as resetting the reactors through the HMI. This Mode block is also connected to the HeartBeat to receive the command to activate Emergency mode in case of a loss of connection between the PLC and the Nereda® Controller.

section.para: Mode is the block that allows the selection of the operating mode (Automatic, Manual, Emergency) as well as resetting the reactors through the HMI. This Mode block is also connected to the HeartBeat to receive the command to activate Emergency mode in case of a loss of connection between the PLC and the Nereda® Controller.

td.para: It gives the state of the connection between the PLC and the Nereda® Controller through the variable EmergencyOn :

listitem.para: EmergencyOn = TRUE : the connection is lost.
EmergencyOn = FALSE : the connection is good.

section.section:
NeredaCAeration Type: CAT Library: SE.Nereda
Nouriddin Ouechen
nouriddin.ouechen@non.se.com
The blower section controls the blowers to provide sufficient air to the reactor during the aeration phase. For Nereda® reactor aeration, two frequency-controlled blowers are installed per reactor. The blower configuration is as follows: one duty blower and one assistance blower per reactor, and the use of one or two blowers is based on the capacity value requested from the Nereda® Reactor.

IAerateReactor01 SE.Nereda.ICommonBlower
IAerateReactor02 SE.Nereda.ICommonBlower
Description : The blower section controls the blowers to provide sufficient air to the reactor during the aeration phase. For Nereda® reactor aeration, two frequency-controlled blowers are installed per reactor. The blower configuration is as follows: one duty blower and one assistance blower per reactor, and the use of one or two blowers is based on the capacity value requested from the Nereda® Reactor. AerationNVPP CAT :
Input Adapters :
Name Type Description
IBlowerReactor
This adapter, 'IDedicatedBlower,' receives start and stop commands through the StartBlower variable, as well as the capacity setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor via the FlowSPBlower variable, and sends the status of the blowers.
Automation: The aeration phase of each reactor sends a START/STOP command and an air capacity setpoint to the blower section. Each reactor will demand a maximum of two blowers.The number of requested blowers (1 or 2) is determined by the capacity setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor. The setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor is in the range of 0 to 100%. The blower capacity has to be scaled to the requested aeration capacity from the Nereda® Reactor.
0% demand from the Nereda® Reactor means 0 Nm³/h.
100% demand from the Nereda® Controller means two blowers at maximum capacity.
Blower capacity < C_MAX => 1 blower operating at the capacity calculated based on the capacity coming from the Nereda® Reactor (114 Nm³/h = max air capacity for 1 blower).
Blower capacity > C_MAX => 2 blowers operating at the capacity calculated based on the capacity coming from the Nereda® Reactor (197 Nm³/h = max air demand reactor).
Based on the start command from the reactor and the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor, the AerationNVPP logic will manage the two blowers as described below:
Single Blower Operation: If the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor is lower than C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint) configured in the aeration settings on the HMI, only one blower will operate at the calculated capacity based on the capacity received from the reactor.
Dual Blower Operation: If the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor exceeds C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint) configured in the aeration settings on the HMI, both blowers will initially start at a capacity of C2 (Starting Blowers Setpoint) or ramp down the running blower to an adjustable capacity of C2 to synchronize their operation. Afterward, the blowers will operate at the calculated capacity based on the capacity received from the Nereda® Reactor.
Transition from Two Blowers to One Blower: If both blowers are operating and the capacity from the Nereda® Controller drops below C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint), the speed of both blowers will reduce to a setpoint of C3 (Below Capacity Setpoint), as defined in the aeration settings on the HMI. then, the system will switch to one blower operating at a speed calculated based on the capacity received from the Nereda® Reactor.

The blower section controls the blowers to provide sufficient air to the reactor during the aeration phase. For Nereda® reactor aeration, two frequency-controlled blowers are installed per reactor. The blower configuration is as follows: one duty blower and one assistance blower per reactor, and the use of one or two blowers is based on the capacity value requested from the Nereda® Reactor.

Description : The blower section controls the blowers to provide sufficient air to the reactor during the aeration phase. For Nereda® reactor aeration, two frequency-controlled blowers are installed per reactor. The blower configuration is as follows: one duty blower and one assistance blower per reactor, and the use of one or two blowers is based on the capacity value requested from the Nereda® Reactor. AerationNVPP CAT :
Input Adapters :
Name Type Description
IBlowerReactor
This adapter, 'IDedicatedBlower,' receives start and stop commands through the StartBlower variable, as well as the capacity setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor via the FlowSPBlower variable, and sends the status of the blowers.
Automation: The aeration phase of each reactor sends a START/STOP command and an air capacity setpoint to the blower section. Each reactor will demand a maximum of two blowers.The number of requested blowers (1 or 2) is determined by the capacity setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor. The setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor is in the range of 0 to 100%. The blower capacity has to be scaled to the requested aeration capacity from the Nereda® Reactor.
0% demand from the Nereda® Reactor means 0 Nm³/h.
100% demand from the Nereda® Controller means two blowers at maximum capacity.
Blower capacity < C_MAX => 1 blower operating at the capacity calculated based on the capacity coming from the Nereda® Reactor (114 Nm³/h = max air capacity for 1 blower).
Blower capacity > C_MAX => 2 blowers operating at the capacity calculated based on the capacity coming from the Nereda® Reactor (197 Nm³/h = max air demand reactor).
Based on the start command from the reactor and the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor, the AerationNVPP logic will manage the two blowers as described below:
Single Blower Operation: If the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor is lower than C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint) configured in the aeration settings on the HMI, only one blower will operate at the calculated capacity based on the capacity received from the reactor.
Dual Blower Operation: If the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor exceeds C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint) configured in the aeration settings on the HMI, both blowers will initially start at a capacity of C2 (Starting Blowers Setpoint) or ramp down the running blower to an adjustable capacity of C2 to synchronize their operation. Afterward, the blowers will operate at the calculated capacity based on the capacity received from the Nereda® Reactor.
Transition from Two Blowers to One Blower: If both blowers are operating and the capacity from the Nereda® Controller drops below C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint), the speed of both blowers will reduce to a setpoint of C3 (Below Capacity Setpoint), as defined in the aeration settings on the HMI. then, the system will switch to one blower operating at a speed calculated based on the capacity received from the Nereda® Reactor.

NeredaSludgeBuffer_2 Type: CAT Library: SE.Nereda
Nouriddin Ouechen
nouriddin.ouechen@non.se.com
The blower section controls the blowers to provide sufficient air to the reactor during the aeration phase. For Nereda® reactor aeration, two frequency-controlled blowers are installed per reactor. The blower configuration is as follows: one duty blower and one assistance blower per reactor, and the use of one or two blowers is based on the capacity value requested from the Nereda® Reactor.

Description : The blower section controls the blowers to provide sufficient air to the reactor during the aeration phase. For Nereda® reactor aeration, two frequency-controlled blowers are installed per reactor. The blower configuration is as follows: one duty blower and one assistance blower per reactor, and the use of one or two blowers is based on the capacity value requested from the Nereda® Reactor. AerationNVPP CAT :
Input Adapters :
Name Type Description
IBlowerReactor
This adapter, 'IDedicatedBlower,' receives start and stop commands through the StartBlower variable, as well as the capacity setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor via the FlowSPBlower variable, and sends the status of the blowers.
Automation: The aeration phase of each reactor sends a START/STOP command and an air capacity setpoint to the blower section. Each reactor will demand a maximum of two blowers.The number of requested blowers (1 or 2) is determined by the capacity setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor. The setpoint from the Nereda® Reactor is in the range of 0 to 100%. The blower capacity has to be scaled to the requested aeration capacity from the Nereda® Reactor.
0% demand from the Nereda® Reactor means 0 Nm³/h.
100% demand from the Nereda® Controller means two blowers at maximum capacity.
Blower capacity < C_MAX => 1 blower operating at the capacity calculated based on the capacity coming from the Nereda® Reactor (114 Nm³/h = max air capacity for 1 blower).
Blower capacity > C_MAX => 2 blowers operating at the capacity calculated based on the capacity coming from the Nereda® Reactor (197 Nm³/h = max air demand reactor).
Based on the start command from the reactor and the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor, the AerationNVPP logic will manage the two blowers as described below:
Single Blower Operation: If the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor is lower than C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint) configured in the aeration settings on the HMI, only one blower will operate at the calculated capacity based on the capacity received from the reactor.
Dual Blower Operation: If the capacity from the Nereda® Reactor exceeds C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint) configured in the aeration settings on the HMI, both blowers will initially start at a capacity of C2 (Starting Blowers Setpoint) or ramp down the running blower to an adjustable capacity of C2 to synchronize their operation. Afterward, the blowers will operate at the calculated capacity based on the capacity received from the Nereda® Reactor.
Transition from Two Blowers to One Blower: If both blowers are operating and the capacity from the Nereda® Controller drops below C_MAX (the Blowers Running Setpoint), the speed of both blowers will reduce to a setpoint of C3 (Below Capacity Setpoint), as defined in the aeration settings on the HMI. then, the system will switch to one blower operating at a speed calculated based on the capacity received from the Nereda® Reactor.
